claude.take: A 30-year-old, backward-integrated maker of solar mounting structures, transmission-line hardware and fasteners that has compounded hard — revenue ₹2,427 Cr to ₹4,316 Cr and PAT ₹103 Cr to ₹229 Cr across FY24-FY26. The catch is price and balance sheet: 32.4x FY26 earnings is above every comparable in the company's own RHP peer table (9.7x-20.5x), while ₹600 of the ₹675 Cr fresh issue merely retires debt against ₹1,344 Cr of borrowings, so shareholders fund deleveraging rather than growth. The ₹310/share pre-IPO placement versus the ₹254 cap, and the halving of the issue from ₹1,750 Cr, both read as a pre-launch valuation reset. GMP ₹40 says the market will take it, but the margin of safety is thin at 5.3% PAT margin.

That is a premium to every peer in its own RHP table — Waaree at 20.5x, Emmvee 18.9x, Saatvik 14.2x, KP Green 9.7x — despite Karamtara being a components/structures supplier rather than a module maker. NAV ₹41.72 means P/B ~6.1x. RoCE 23.27% and PAT margin 5.30% are respectable for a fabrication business, but the multiple leaves little room if solar capex ordering slows.
